look for marked dilatation (tracheobronchomegaly) extending into the lobar bronchi.", "Evaluate the morphology of the cystic spaces on axial CT; identify large, thin-walled diverticula or cysts that appear contiguous with the dilated airways, often containing air-fluid levels due to poor clearance.", "Distinguish from Williams-Campbell syndrome by confirming the trachea and main bronchi are involved (dilated), whereas Williams-Campbell typically presents with normal proximal airways and dilation restricted to distal segmental/subsegmental bronchi.", "Distinguish from Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis (ABPA) by noting the absence of central bronchiectasis with high-attenuation mucus plugging and lack of peripheral eosinophilic infiltrates;
